standard_prerequisites.name: Sigma type over a family of mere propositions
standard_prerequisites.statement: The type consists of a point of the base together with an element of a family that is assumed to be a family of mere propositions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type whose elements are compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: Paths in a Sigma type
standard_prerequisites.statement: A path between two pairs is given by a path between the first components together with a path between the transported second component and the second component of the target.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the criterion that reduces the goal to one equation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mere proposition
standard_prerequisites.statement: Any two elements of a mere proposition are equal.

core_obligations: Assume a path between the first components of the two pairs (source lines 472-472).

Use the path criterion for Sigma types to reduce the goal to the equality of the transported second component with the second component of the target, at the appropriate point of the base (source lines 473-473).
Conclude that equality because both sides lie in the same proposition of the family, which is a mere proposition (source lines 474-474).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the pair equality to one equation by the Sigma path criterion.
Close it by propositionality of the family.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 467-470 (book Lemma 3.5.1): for a family of mere propositions, two elements of the Sigma type whose first components are equal are equal. The statement looks like a formality but the proof (source lines 471-475) has to invoke the path criterion for Sigma types, which turns the pair equality into the equation between the transported second component and the target component at the right point of the base, and then to notice that both sides of that equation live in one proposition of the family, which is where the hypothesis is used. The transport step and the choice of the point at which the equation is formulated are invisible in the statement.
